name: bettyapp-teachers
description: Find free educational lecture clips for your lessons. Bettyapp searches indexed lecture moments, finds explanations matched to your topic and teaching level, and provides playback links, curriculum information and source attribution. Build lessons around real video explanations in ChatGPT.

interface.longDescription:
Find free educational lecture clips for your lessons. Bettyapp searches indexed lecture moments, finds explanations matched to your topic and teaching level, and provides playback links, curriculum information and source attribution. Build lessons around real video explanations in ChatGPT.

Ask for a topic and the class's level, such as the chain rule for a Grade 12 class. Bettyapp finds the few minutes inside a long lecture where it is taught, such as minutes 28 to 33 of an MIT calculus lecture, and returns: where each clip starts and a suggested end, the lecture and its teacher, how the moment treats the topic, and the clip's credit line and licence. Ask for a course, such as Ontario's Grade 12 Physics (SPH4U) or England's GCSE Biology, for its topics in order with their codes and a clip for each. Ask what to teach before a topic and after it, or for the same topic at each level.

Bettyapp gives the facts; ChatGPT writes the lesson plan around them.

For high school and first-year university teachers first. The lectures come from open courses, such as MIT OpenCourseWare and Oak National Academy, and from teachers who publish on YouTube.

Limitations: Bettyapp finds only the lectures it has, and says so when it has none on a topic. Its tools only read Bettyapp's lecture catalogue: they change nothing and keep no account. It asks for no student names, grades or work.
capabilities: Find lecture clips that teach a topic, with a start and a suggested end
Give a course's topics in order, with their codes and a clip for each
List the curricula and courses Bettyapp follows
Suggest the topics to teach before and after a topic
Give a topic at each level, from school to university
defaultPrompt: Find a few minutes from a university lecture where the chain rule is worked through on an example, for my Grade 12 class.
Find a few minutes of a university chemistry lecture that explain entropy with a concrete example, for first-year students.
Find a few minutes of a real lecture on when natural selection can and cannot happen, for my university biology class.

positive.description: Find the minutes inside a long lecture that teach a topic, for a class's level.
positive.prompt: Find a few minutes from a university lecture where the chain rule is worked through on an example, for my Grade 12 calculus class.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_teaching_clips for the chain rule. Offers recommended clips judged to teach it, such as Applying the chain rule to sine to the 10th in MIT 18.01 Lecture 04: Chain rule. Higher derivatives, from 28:03 to about 33:44 of the 46-minute lecture, with the link that plays it from 28:03 on bettyapp.org, the credit line (MIT OpenCourseWare) and a licence note (CC BY-NC-SA).

positive.description: A concrete example of a hard idea, an hour into a university lecture.
positive.prompt: Find a few minutes from a real university chemistry lecture that explain entropy with a concrete example, for my first-year students.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_teaching_clips for entropy. Offers recommended clips judged to teach it, such as Entropy change when ice melts in UC Irvine General Chemistry 1B Lecture 7, from 1:00:40 to about 1:02:48, and Entropy as a measure of disorder in MIT Lecture 16, from 11:37 to about 14:26, each with its link, credit line and licence note.

positive.description: The curricula Bettyapp follows, then one course.
positive.prompt: Which exam boards and curricula does Bettyapp follow? Then show me the first topics of England's GCSE Biology.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_curricula and names boards and curricula it returns, such as Ontario, OCR, Cambridge International, England and Singapore. Then calls find_by_curriculum for England GCSE Biology and lists its first topics in order, such as Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cell structure with a Crash Course clip and Mitosis and the cell cycle with a Khan Academy clip.

positive.description: A few minutes of a university lecture for a teacher preparing a class.
positive.prompt: I'm about to teach evolution by natural selection to my university biology students. Find a few minutes of a real lecture that explain when natural selection can and cannot happen.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_teaching_clips for natural selection. Offers the clip When natural selection cannot happen in Open Yale Courses' 1. The Nature of Evolution: Selection, Inheritance, and History (Stephen Stearns), from 17:48 to about 22:50 of the 43-minute lecture, with its link, credit line and licence note.

positive.prompt: I teach Singapore's Secondary 3 Physics. Find clips for the first topics of the Measurement unit.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls find_by_curriculum for Singapore Secondary Physics with the unit Measurement. Lists its topics in order with their syllabus codes, such as Physical quantities and SI units (1(a)–(c)) with a Khan Academy clip, and says where Bettyapp has none.

negative.description: Student data: Bettyapp asks for none and takes none.
negative.prompt: Here are my students' names and their test marks. Which of them should watch the photosynthesis clip again?
negative.expected_behavior: Sends no student names or marks to Bettyapp and calls no Bettyapp tool with them. It may offer a photosynthesis clip for the whole class.

negative.prompt: Book a meeting with my students' parents for Thursday afternoon.

negative.description: A change to Bettyapp: the tools only read the lecture catalogue.
negative.prompt: Upload my own lecture video to Bettyapp and add it to my course.
negative.expected_behavior: Calls no Bettyapp tool, and says that this can't be done from ChatGPT.

review.commerce_description: Bettyapp sells nothing in ChatGPT and links to no checkout.

publication.release_notes: Finds the few minutes inside a long lecture that teach your topic, from universities such as MIT, UC Irvine and Yale, with where each clip starts and a suggested end, its curriculum codes, credit line and licence note.
